models: Signed 16-bit integer, from -32768 through 32767. Cleaning rejects overflow and fractional input.
Signed 32-bit integer. Use BigIntegerField when the value can exceed the 32-bit range.
Signed 64-bit integer. Preserve integers as integers or exact JSON numbers; float conversion can lose precision.
Nonnegative signed-small-integer storage. Zero is accepted; negative and overflowing values fail.
Nonnegative signed-32-bit storage. Positive means nonnegative here, not strictly greater than zero.
Nonnegative signed-64-bit storage. Use WithBounds to impose a stricter business minimum or maximum.
Database-allocated small identity. The constructor sets PrimaryKey=true and Editable=false. Omit the value on an insert; use a separate schema for each alternative identity type.
Database-allocated standard identity. The constructor sets PrimaryKey=true and Editable=false; scalar cleaning alone does not allocate an ID.
Database-allocated large identity. Noneditable primary key by default. A successful insert, not the declaration, provides the persisted identity.
UUID text validation. Does not generate a UUID automatically; supply WithDefaultFunc with a stable ID if your application owns generation.

Exact decimal string with 12 total digits and two fractional digits in this example. MaxDigits must be positive; DecimalPlaces must be between zero and MaxDigits. Excess scale is rejected, not rounded.
Finite approximate floating-point value. NaN and infinities are invalid; choose Decimal for exact monetary values.
Model boolean; false is valid and distinct from absence. Unlike a required Boolean form field, this does not require affirmative consent.
String with explicit length bounds. Bounds count Unicode code points. WithMaxLength(0) leaves the validation maximum unset; database mapping and migration constraints remain separate.
String for longer text. No implicit maximum length; add WithMinLength/WithMaxLength and custom validators as needed.

ASCII letters, digits, underscore and hyphen by default. Constructor sets MaxLength=50 and DBIndex=true. WithAllowUnicode(true) admits Unicode letters/numbers, but does not transliterate, normalize or generate a value. UniqueValue is an explicit additional choice.
Bare email-address validation; display-name mailbox syntax is rejected. Does not verify mailbox ownership or send email.
URL scalar validation with supported scheme/host rules. Does not fetch the URL or make it a safe server-side network destination.
IPv4/IPv6 parsing and canonicalization. An accepted address is data, not an authorization to connect to it.
String-like path metadata. Does not enumerate a filesystem, check existence or confine access to a storage root.
Calendar date. Invalid calendar dates fail; do not treat a date as a timezone-independent timestamp for an event.
Timestamp/instant cleaning. The example supplies an explicit UTC offset; localized wall-time input belongs to configured form/timezone handling.
Wall-clock time, not an instant. Hour 25 is invalid; database precision and date components must not be inferred from the input display.
Go duration value. PostgreSQL interval round trips use microsecond precision; this is elapsed duration, not a calendar-month count.
Byte-slice data. No automatic form mapping; supply an explicit form/API representation and bound uploads separately.
Native JSON-compatible values; json.RawMessage explicitly opts into parsing. Use json.Number for exact large numbers. JSON shape validation is separate from domain authorization.
Opaque storage-key string. Does not upload, validate bytes, check object availability or authorize a download.
Opaque image storage-key string. Model cleaning does not decode image bytes; use a bounded upload validator and an explicit file service.
Many rows reference one registered target. Relation metadata is required. Scalar Clean does not establish existence or permission; registry resolution, scoped lookup and database checks do that.
Foreign-key relation with Unique=true by default. Target lookup and concurrent database uniqueness are separate from descriptor construction.
Intermediary-table relation, not a stored scalar column. Configure explicit Through/ThroughFields when needed. Self-relations default to symmetrical; use a false pointer for directed links.
func() models.Field { f := models.NewField("value", models.Generated); element := models.IntegerField("element"); f.Element = &element; f.GeneratedExpression = "1 + 1"; return f }()
Noneditable generated-column descriptor. Requires trusted expression and supported backend type metadata. Not an ordinary writable field or proof of generated-value round-trip support.
func() models.Field { f := models.NewField("value", models.Array); element := models.IntegerField("element"); f.Element = &element; return f }()
Requires Element metadata; scalar cleaning validates each element. PostgreSQL type mapping is not a guarantee of array ORM codecs, Admin editing or serializer support.
PostgreSQL key/value descriptor requiring extension:hstore capability. No full HStore value-codec, CRUD or Admin editing guarantee.
func() models.Field { f := models.NewField("value", models.Range); f.RangeType = models.Integer; return f }()
Range type metadata; this example maps an integer range. Does not implement a general range value codec or complete CRUD workflow.
PostgreSQL tsvector storage vocabulary. Does not by itself provide document indexing, ranking or a complete search API.
PostGIS-gated geometry type metadata only. Complete spatial queries, codecs and GIS widgets are not implemented.
PostGIS-gated geography type metadata only. Does not implement geodesic operations, complete codecs or map widgets.
PostGIS-gated raster metadata. No complete raster codec, processing pipeline or Admin raster editor.
Application-owned field descriptor. Supply codec, validation, backend and presentation support explicitly; the stock PostgreSQL dialect/default form mapping reject unsupported custom kinds.
forms: Trims whitespace by default. Set Strip to a pointer to false to preserve spaces. MinLength/MaxLength count Unicode code points.
Required=true demands an affirmative checkbox. Set Required=false for an ordinary optional boolean. False, empty input and zero text are false values.
Accepts true/false and unknown as nil. Required rejects the unknown state; an optional field retains nil.
func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.ChoiceKind); f.Choices = []forms.Choice{{Value: "one", Label: "One"}}; return f }()
One string value from Choices. Labels do not change the submitted value. Unknown values fail invalid_choice.

func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.TypedChoice); f.Choices = []forms.Choice{{Value: "1", Label: "One"}}; f.Coerce = func(v string) (any, error) { return strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64) }; return f }()
Checks choice membership before Coerce converts the string to an application value. Coercion errors are input errors.
func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.MultipleChoice); f.Choices = []forms.Choice{{Value: "one", Label: "One"}}; return f }()
Multiple strings from Choices. Submit repeated values under the same field name; every selection must be allowed.

func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.TypedMultipleChoice); f.Choices = []forms.Choice{{Value: "1", Label: "One"}}; f.Coerce = func(v string) (any, error) { return strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64) }; return f }()
Multiple allowed values, each converted with Coerce after membership checks. Configure both Choices and Coerce.
Parses integer input, rejecting fractional values. MinValue and MaxValue are optional inclusive numeric bounds.
Parses a finite floating-point value. NaN and infinities are rejected; use Decimal for exact decimals.
func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.Decimal); f.MaxDigits, f.DecimalPlaces = 8, 2; return f }()
Requires explicit digit/scale limits for predictable validation. Returns a decimal string; excess fractional digits fail instead of rounding.
Calendar date parsing. Default layout is 2006-01-02; InputFormats can supply explicit accepted Go layouts.
Timestamp or configured local wall-time parsing. InputFormats uses Go layouts; timezone policy comes from form context.
Time-of-day parsing, not an absolute timestamp. Configure InputFormats for alternate accepted layouts.
Parses Go duration syntax, such as 1h2m. Does not interpret arbitrary phrases or calendar months.
Bare email-address validation; display-name syntax is rejected. Validation does not verify delivery or ownership.
Supported scheme/host validation; javascript URLs are invalid. This is not SSRF authorization for fetching the address.
UUID parsing and normalization. Does not generate a missing UUID automatically.
ASCII slug characters by default; AllowUnicode widens letters/numbers. No implicit prepopulation, transliteration or uniqueness check.
IPv4/IPv6 parsing and normalization. Invalid addresses fail validation.
func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.Regex); f.Pattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^DEMO-[0-9]+$`); return f }()
Requires a compiled Pattern. Anchor the pattern to enforce a whole-input match; ErrorMessages can customize invalid feedback.
Bounded JSON decoding with json.Number so large numeric values are not silently converted to float64. Trailing content is rejected.
func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.File); f.MaxBytes = 4096; return f }()
Requires multipart file input supplied with WithFiles, not a text filename. Set MaxBytes and bound HTTP parsing; successful validation does not store the bytes.
func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.Image); f.MaxBytes = 4096; return f }()
Checks bounded uploaded image data. Supply multipart input with WithFiles; validation does not create a persisted storage object.
String cleaning only. No filesystem enumeration, path confinement or file-existence authorization is implemented by this field.

func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.ModelChoice); f.Resolve = func(ctx context.Context, ids []string) ([]any, error) { return nil, fmt.Errorf("replace with scoped lookup") }; return f }()
Requires Resolve to look up and authorize one submitted relation ID. This declaration intentionally denies until you supply a real scoped resolver.

func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.ModelMultipleChoice); f.Resolve = func(ctx context.Context, ids []string) ([]any, error) { return nil, fmt.Errorf("replace with scoped lookup") }; return f }()
Requires an authorized Resolve callback for every submitted ID. Duplicate IDs are deduplicated; UI labels are not proof of permission. The example denies until wired.
func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.MultiValue); f.Fields = []forms.Field{forms.NewField("first", forms.Integer), forms.NewField("second", forms.Integer)}; return f }()
Cleans component fields independently. Submit value_0/value_1; optional Compress combines the cleaned components into a domain value.

func() forms.Field { f := forms.NewField("value", forms.Combo); pattern := forms.NewField("pattern", forms.Regex); pattern.Pattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^DEMO-[0-9]+$`); f.Fields = []forms.Field{forms.NewField("text", forms.Char), pattern}; return f }()
Runs one value through component cleaners in order; this example applies Char then Regex validation.
Defaults to separate Date and Time components. Submit value_0 and value_1; combines them using configured locale/timezone policy.
serializers: String input using model Char cleaning. Variadic model options configure bounds, choices and null/blank behavior; serializer direction flags are configured on the returned api.Field.
Uses the model BigInteger cleaner, not the narrower model Integer kind. Keep large values exact when decoding JSON.
Boolean input; false is valid, unlike an affirmative required form checkbox. Missing and explicit null are separate conditions.
Exact decimal string with explicit total digits and fractional places. Excess precision fails instead of rounding or converting through float64.
Finite approximate floating-point scalar. Supports model field options; NaN and infinity are rejected.
UUID scalar validation. No implicit identifier generation; add an explicit trusted default if required.
Supported URL syntax/scheme validation. Does not fetch the resource or authorize server-side network access.
Bare email address validation, not mailbox verification. Model length/choice/custom-validation options can be supplied.
Uses model Slug validation; default maximum is 50. Unicode acceptance is explicit and never means automatic slug generation or transliteration.
Model IP-address normalization under the serializer constructor name IPAddressField. Supports IPv4 and IPv6 input.
Calendar date scalar. Date semantics differ from DateTime instants; an invalid calendar date fails validation.
Timestamp scalar with explicit offset in the example. Output formatting and OpenAPI representation follow the serializer's declared wire behavior.
Wall-clock time scalar, not a date or absolute instant. Rejects invalid time-of-day values.
Duration scalar using model normalization. Keep it distinct from a calendar period or timestamp.
JSON-compatible structured value. Use json.Number for exact numbers; use nested serializers for declared domain shapes instead of accepting arbitrary JSON.

Required list with an Element declaration and explicit maximum item count. Zero maximum becomes 1000. Set direction flags on the parent, not the element; nested objects belong inside an element serializer.
String-keyed dictionary with a validated Element value and item-count bound. MinItems/MaxItems constrain entry count, not byte size; also bound HTTP input.
func() api.Field { child, err := api.New(api.Definition{Fields: []api.Field{api.StringField("name")}}); if err != nil { panic(err) }; return api.NestedField("value", child) }()
Required nested object validated by an explicit child serializer. It does not create/update nested database records; persistence and graph authorization remain your policy's responsibility.
api.ComputedField("value", func(ctx context.Context, record api.ValueReader) (any, error) { return "computed", nil })
Read-only output callback. Does not accept caller values as writable input. Supply OutputSchema when generating an unambiguous output schema for a custom computation.
Wraps an existing scalar declaration with allowed model choice values. It does not replace the wrapped type or use labels as values.
Required, write-only multipart FileHeader input. Zero maxBytes becomes 10 MiB. Rejects empty/oversized files and unsafe names; does not store bytes or create an output URL.
File validation plus decoded image dimension checks. Zero limits become 10 MiB and 40 million pixels. Write-only by default; a header check is not a full malware scan or storage operation.

Reuses one model field's scalar normalization. Required derives from Blank/default metadata and AllowNull from Null; model registration/editability does not automatically define public read/write permissions.
